title: st_read excel the first row as data
body: ### What happens? I have two excel, use st_read, one is OK, another read the first row as data rather than header. `OGR_XLSX_HEADERS=FORCE duckdb`

on the command line and you'll find the environment variable will then be in effect.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Try launching dbeaver from the command line:

`OGR_XLSX_HEADERS=FORCE /Applications/DBeaver.app/Contents/MacOS/dbeaver`

You could also write a little shell script which has the above command and then double-click it from Finder.

It's far from ideal to rely on environment variables to set these options for st_read().  I would love to be able to set them via the "open_options" of the st_read() function.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I've made fix in https://github.com/duckdblabs/duckdb_spatial/pull/114 so that you can choose to force reading the first row as header or not by passing an option from within duckdb. This works with the excel file provided.

![image](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/assets/1337636/bd86050b-d915-4358-95ac-599f547d933a)

Note that while this is now merged it is __not part of the nightly builds distributed by duckdb__ yet. We may do an update in a week or so, otherwise it will be present in duckdb 0.9.0 which is scheduled for September.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body: I don't understand what the behaviour you want is. By default, it will guess, but as I showed above you can explicitly disable reading headers by passing `open_options=['HEADERS=DISABLE']);`. Or you can also explicitly force reading headers by passing `open_options=['HEADERS=FORCE'];`. In the image below I show how you can do both.
